passage: Two weeks after the apology, Mansi agreed to meet Dhruv for chai at the stall near Churchgate. She half expected him to be late. He was already there, ten minutes early, with two cutting chais going cold. "You said you hate the ginger one," he said, sliding her the plain one. And later: "How did the interview go? The one you were scared about?" She'd mentioned it once, weeks ago. He had remembered. They talked for an hour. Walking back to the station, Mansi realised she hadn't checked her phone once to see if he'd cancel. It wasn't the sorry that had done it. It was the plain chai and the question about the interview.

qa.q: Which chai did Dhruv give Mansi?
qa.a: He slid her the plain one, because she hates the ginger one.

qa.q: What did Mansi half expect before meeting Dhruv?
qa.a: She half expected him to be late, which shows her trust was still shaky.

qa.q: What rebuilt trust here more than the apology?
qa.a: Small actions matching his words: arriving early, remembering she hates ginger chai, and asking about her interview.

qa.q: How might Dhruv feel as the evening goes well?
qa.a: He probably feels relieved and hopeful, seeing that showing up and remembering are slowly earning back her trust. 😊

grounding: Shows a young man proving his apology by arriving on time and remembering what his friend cares about, which rebuilds her trust.

passage:
"Shankar's outside again," her brother Lokesh called from the window. "Right on time. Third Sunday in a row."
Lakshmi picked up her badminton racket. "I know."
"After the way he kept bailing last month? You forgave him fast."
"I didn't forgive him fast. He said sorry a month ago, and I told him I'd believe it when I saw it."
"And?"
"And he's been here at eight every Sunday. He brought shuttlecocks because I said ours were falling apart. He asked about Amma's knee."
"That's it? Shuttlecocks?"
"That's it." Lakshmi smiled at the door. "Sorry is one day. This is three Sundays. It adds up."
Outside, the horn beeped twice, politely.

qa.q: What did Shankar bring for Lakshmi?
qa.a: He brought shuttlecocks because she said theirs were falling apart.

qa.q: Why does Lakshmi smile at the door?
qa.a: She feels her trust returning because Shankar's actions have matched his words for three Sundays.

qa.q: Which choice worked for Shankar, and why?
qa.a: Showing up on time every week and remembering small things worked, because repeated actions prove an apology far more than saying sorry again.

qa.q: How does Lokesh first see Lakshmi's attitude to Shankar?
qa.a: Lokesh thinks she forgave Shankar too fast, not seeing that trust came back slowly through three Sundays of actions.

grounding: Shows trust returning as a young man keeps showing up on time and remembering what his friend cares about, week after week.
